code_findings.title: For an existing settings file, when LoadedSettings.setValue replaces a string at a tracked environment-variable path with another string and that path is not altered by migration, the save writes the
code_findings.explanation: Loading records each resolved environment-backed string by path and retains its original reference. setValue changes the in-memory setting but passes the unchanged mapping to saveSettings. applyUpdates first places the new literal into the parsed file structure, but restoreEnvVarsRecursive then looks up only the path and replaces any string there with the original reference. Although mappings contain resolvedValue, restoration never compares the current value with it. The resulting file is explicitly written after this replacement, so the new literal does not persist.
code_findings.impact: Caused by the change: This change introduced persistent load-time mappings and made setValue pass them into the new format-preserving save path. Because the restoration map retains only mapping.originalValue keyed by path, the newly assigned literal is overwritten at that path before serialization. The stored resolvedValue is not consulted, so restoration cannot distinguish an unchanged resolved secret from an intentional replacement literal.

code_findings.title: For MCP configurations containing both a server named `foo.headers` with header `API` and a server named `foo` with header `headers.API`, distinct environment-reference paths flatten to the same map k
code_findings.explanation: The MCP add path stores server names and header names directly as object keys, so dotted names can coexist: `foo.headers` and `foo` are distinct server keys, while `API` and `headers.API` are valid header keys. Their component paths are respectively `['mcpServers','foo.headers','headers','API']` and `['mcpServers','foo','headers','headers.API']`, but both join to `mcpServers.foo.headers.headers.API`. The changed restoration code inserts mappings into a Map under this joined string, so one mapping overwrites the other. Recursive restoration constructs the same joined key for both leaves and therefore applies the surviving reference to both. If the original references differ, such as `$A` and `$B`, at least one field is restored incorrectly.
code_findings.impact: Caused by the change: This change introduces environment-reference restoration keyed by dot-joined paths. The supported MCP keys produce two distinct component paths with the same joined representation; Map insertion discards one mapping, and recursive lookup then uses the remaining reference for both settings. The prior direct save did not perform this ambiguous restoration.

pr_semantic_analysis.change_summary: CLI settings persistence now parses and rewrites existing settings through comment-json, retaining comments and existing document structure while restoring tracked environment-variable references instead of always replacing the file with plain JSON. Loading now records environment substitutions per settings scope so later writes can avoid persisting resolved values.

behavior_changes.description: When an existing valid settings file is saved, it is parsed, updated in place, and serialized through comment-json. This is intended to retain comments; keys not represented in the supplied update also remain in the document rather than being removed by a full-file replacement.
evidence: saveSettings delegates persistence to the new format-preserving updater.
The updater starts from the parsed existing document and applies only entries present in the update object.
The added test expects existing comments to remain after an update.

behavior_changes.description: Settings originally expressed as a single environment-variable reference are tracked during loading and changed back to that reference when the corresponding scope is saved, avoiding persistence of the resolved string value in the ordinary case.
evidence: Loading clones each scope before environment resolution and records differences matching environment-reference syntax.
LoadedSettings carries the per-scope mappings into saveSettings.
The writer replaces string values at mapped paths with the original reference before serialization.

local_risks.description: A setting that was an environment reference when loaded cannot reliably be changed to a new literal string through setValue: the saved value is passed with the old scope mapping, and restoration replaces any string at that path with the original reference without checking whether it still equals the previously resolved value. The in-memory setting can therefore differ from what is persisted.

Environment references nested inside arrays can be tracked but not restored. Tracking descends into every non-null object, including arrays, while restoration explicitly declines to recurse into array values; if such a reference resolves to a secret, saving can write the resolved value to disk.

The new updater never removes an existing key merely because it is absent from settingsToSave; it mutates the parsed document by iterating only supplied entries. If saveSettings supplies the desired complete snapshot, setting removal or migration cleanup will not be persisted and stale configuration can remain active.
